summary: Slow chat session handshake and delayed first token following runtime ABI alignment and model merge
description:
Issue summary: BrightHealth AI reports a sudden increase in chat time-to-first-token (TTFB) across multiple sessions after we merged a runtime ABI alignment and a model catalog consolidation on 2026-03-09. Impact: Customers experience 2–6s additional delay before first token, intermittent streaming stalls, and a small number of 504s on chat endpoints. This impacts latency-sensitive product flows for an enterprise customer on a reserved Dedicated pool.

Environment: Production us-east serving cluster handling BrightHealth enterprise Dedicated pool (dedicated tenant, pinned model redwood-open-14b-v1). The runtime and model merge deployment occurred 2026-03-09 03:00 UTC (deploy tag runtime-1.8.0, modelset-v2026-03-09).

Observed behavior: After the deploy, median TTFB increased from ~120ms to ~2.3s for initial tokens on warm sessions; 95th percentile increased to ~5.7s. Errors: increased transient 504s correlated with long handshake windows. The regression is more visible for multi-turn conversations that rely on KV cache warmup.

Expected behavior: No significant TTFB change for pinned models or Dedicated customers after compatibility-only ABI alignment. Streaming should begin immediately once the first tokens are emitted.

Impact classification: Customer-visible latency regression for an enterprise customer on Dedicated capacity; classified as Sev1 (service degradation with business impact).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Using BrightHealth AI tenant in prod-us-east with pinned model redwood-open-14b-v1, open a new chat session via /v1/chat/completions
2) Send a multi-turn conversation payload (system prompt + 2 user messages, total ~250 tokens) with streaming=true
3) Observe time between request acceptance (200) and first streaming event (first token chunk) using ttfb timing from client
4) Repeat across several sessions and compare before/after deploy baselines (runtime-1.7.6 vs runtime-1.8.0)
5) Optionally force a cold session by evicting KV cache for that tenant via /admin/cache/evict (for internal repro)

comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reported first-byte delays that started after our 2026-03-09 runtime/model merge. They see 2–6s stalls and sometimes 504s. Asked for request IDs and affected model.

2026-03-10 10:45 - Marco Li (SRE): Observed elevated ttfb spikes for tenant brighthealth in prod-us-east. Correlated with runtime-1.8.0 deploy and a compatibility shim that invalidates older KV cache entries. Opening investigation.
2026-03-10 14:05 - BrightHealth (Customer): Provided request ids and a short sample session. Emphasized user-facing impact and urgent SLA requirement. Requested ETA for mitigation.

2026-03-11 09:30 - Marco Li (SRE): Ran canary repro with cache-evict and saw consistent ~2.1s kv_cache_lookup step. Hypothesis: ABI alignment introduced an extra validation pass which blocks token emission until KV lookup confirms compatibility.

2026-03-11 16:20 - Runtime Eng (Elena Gomez): Confirmed PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4721 added an ABI compatibility layer that performs model metadata checksum checks during session init. Reasonable for safety but adds synchronous IO paths.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: ABI compatibility shim performs synchronous model metadata validation and triggers allocator small-block fallback when pinned model binary layout differs -> adds ~1.5–2.5s to session_init.
Hypothesis 2: KV cache key format changed due to model merge (modelset-v2026-03-09) leading to cache miss storm and additional disk reads for cold/resident tenants.
Telemetry: Sampling of 200 slow sessions shows 92% had a long 'kv_cache_lookup' stage and 18% included a grpc keepalive reset event. No clear network-level packet loss in cloud provider telemetry.
Repro: Internal canary with tenant zzz-test recreated regression when compatibility checks enabled; disabling checksum validation reduced median TTFB back to ~130ms.
Risk: Disabling compatibility checks globally could allow serving mismatch for older pinned models; need targeted mitigation for Dedicated customers with pinned models.
Next steps: prepare targeted hotfix to short-circuit checksum for pinned Dedicated tenants and add async validation for non-blocking path; propose rollback window if hotfix causes failures.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 02:00 - Rolled out hotfix release runtime-1.8.1 to prod-us-east for Dedicated tenant path: compatibility shim now performs async checksum when tenant has pinned model and serving-grade flag is set.
2026-03-12 02:20 - BrightHealth reported immediate improvement: median TTFB returned to ~140ms and 95th to ~420ms. No further 504s observed after hotfix.

Follow-up: Engineering to land PR to make async validation default with feature flag and add telemetry to detect KV cache format mismatches proactively. Confluence runbook updated with rollback steps and customer communication template.

Postmortem action items: 1) Add unit/integration test around ABI alignment path and KV cache compatibility; 2) Implement non-blocking validator for future model merges; 3) Add a Dedicated-tenant preflight that runs compatibility checks at deploy time (not at session init).
